sourceObservations.observations: Lecture 34 title: Fundamentals of Neural Networks. Footer 1; no technical content.
Learning-objective list: biological history, perceptron, activations, architecture, forward/loss/backprop/gradient descent, training and robotic applications. Footer 2; technical details occur later.

Timeline associates 1958 perceptron/Unimate, 1986 backprop/grippers, 1998 LeNet/vision pick-place, 2012 AlexNet/DARPA, 2016 policy gradient/dexterity, 2020 transformers/RT-1 and 2023+ LLM vision. Associations are printed schematic history, not verified invention dates; Unimate deployment, transformer origins and RT-1 dates need qualification rather than silent acceptance.

Four sensor inputs (touch, pixel, IMU, mic) feed weighted sum plus bias, f(z), action. Analogy maps dendrite to robot sensor, cell body to microcontroller, synapse to wire/CAN bus, axon to motor signal and threshold to trigger voltage. This is a computational analogy, not equivalence to biological mechanisms or automatically calibrated sensor importance.
MP unit uses binary inputs and manually chosen inclusive threshold; sum has implicit unit coefficients, not learned weights. Dates 1943 and named authors appear.
Fictional three-feature patient example maps looking fine, normal voice, verbal confirmation to a binary output. This page gives no threshold and is not clinical validation.
Threshold two fires on all three ones; equal unit input contributions are meant by no weights. The toy rule is not a trained diagnostic model.
Source conflates real-valued inputs and linear separability and wrongly attributes perceptron refinement/invention to the 1969 Minsky/Papert book. Neither assertion is adopted unqualified.
Perceptron diagram includes learnable weights, augmented x0=1 and w0=-theta, and inclusive step of the augmented sum. Three pictured features do not limit general n.
Displayed threshold algebra becomes additive bias through x0=1, w0=-theta. Boundary shift depends on fixed weights; origin distance depends on bias divided by weight norm.
Comparison shows fixed equal MP coefficients versus learnable unequal perceptron weights and bias. Binary classification describes individual units, not all architectures.
Positive set P uses target one and negative set N zero. Correctly classified examples leave weights unchanged. Convergence claim needs separable finite data and suitable updates/visits.

Actual inset includes both positive-error addition and negative-error subtraction, including score zero in negative branch. Dot-product angle requires nonzero vectors. Adding x improves its own score by squared norm but need not immediately fix classification or increase every coordinate.

Step is already nonlinear but has zero derivative away from threshold and undefined derivative at threshold. Sigmoid and tanh formulas/plots shown. Multiple identity-activated affine layers remain affine.

Printed closed sigmoid/tanh ranges need open finite-input endpoints in exact arithmetic. Softmax normalizes mutually exclusive logits; binary sigmoid and independent multilabel sigmoids remain valid distinct choices. Tanh zero-centeredness is not universal superiority.

Backprop multiplies activation derivatives and weight factors. Sigmoid maximum derivative is one quarter, while tanh reaches one at zero despite source grouping. ReLU-family alternatives mitigate, not universally eliminate, vanishing gradients.

Actual table shows ReLU=max(0,x), leaky=max(.01x,x), GELU=x Phi(x). ReLU and leaky have a kink at zero; GELU minimum near -.17 is rounded. The solution title and prevention language should not imply every full-network gradient is protected.

Architecture diagram has three inputs, four hidden nodes and one output. With one bias per non-input node there are 21 scalars. Formula is first-hidden-layer affine transform plus ReLU; one versus multiple hidden layers defines the stated shallow/deep distinction.

Output formula is sigmoid(W2 a1+b2). Hidden nonlinearities learn representations; output activation matches the prediction format. Number of output units equals number of encoded outputs, not universally number of binary class labels.
Four-stage training schematic explicitly orders forward pass, loss calculation, backpropagation and gradient descent update; the last two are distinct operations.
Forward pass computes z=sum wi xi+b then f(z); explicit b replaces augmented w0. No learning refers to fixed-parameter feedforward computation, not every possible stateful model execution.

Loss compares predictions to labels and guides training; source says training only, but held-out labeled evaluation can compute loss without updating. Cross-entropy/classification and MSE/regression are common choices, not exclusive mathematical domains.

Both printed cross-entropy sums visibly omit the leading minus. The multiclass loss is also called Softmax, conflating normalization and objective. MSE averages squared errors. i indexes examples, j classes.

Source groups derivative calculation, backward propagation and descent into a broad training explanation. Backprop computes derivatives; optimizer updates parameters. Negative-gradient direction is locally descending only with suitable step size.

Weights/biases are parameters and eta a hyperparameter. Single-sample half-squared loss is an explicit rescaling, not n=1 substitution into ordinary MSE. Half factor simplifies derivative coefficients, not differentiability.
Chain rule derives (yhat-y)*x and yhat-y for an identity-output affine model with half-squared loss. Nonlinear output would require an additional activation derivative.

Update equations subtract eta times derivatives and iterate until the chosen loss stopping criterion. A loss plateau does not certify a global optimum or generalization. Visualization link is supplemental.

Toy braking example gives x=2 m, target10 Nm, initial w3,b1 and eta.1. Dimensional parameter scaling matters; one observation leaves infinitely many affine fits and cannot establish a safe braking controller.
Affine prediction3*2+1=7 and half-squared loss4.5 are shown. Slide calls this MSE though ordinary one-example MSE is9; scaling must remain explicit.
Both gradients evaluated at the old state are -6 for w and -3 for b. The intuition to increase w is specific to this residual/input and a sufficiently small step.
Simultaneous update gives w3.6,b1.3. Next prediction8.5 has half-loss1.125. Epoch2 labels the second evaluation after only one update.

Actual static graph shows only initial y=3x+1 and loss4.5 at epoch1, despite prose promising five-epoch trend. Graph labels Motor Speed whereas earlier example specifies braking torque. The separately linked notebook is now read as original source, not an author answer key.

CNN digit diagram explicitly shows input28x28, first pooling12x12, second convolution8x8, second pooling4x4, flatten, fully connected ten neurons, output example7. Kernel sizes/channel counts are not printed; any inference needs supplied padding/stride assumptions.

Recurrent block takes xt and h(t-1), emits yt and ht. The temporal-summary analogy is not exact indefinite recall. Applications include trajectory prediction, speech and IMU sequences; no LSTM gate equations are printed.

Actual Transformer diagram includes positional encoding, shifted-right decoder input, masked self-attention, encoder-to-decoder attention, Add&Norm blocks, Nx repetition and linear/softmax output. Order is not irrelevant despite loose prose; VLA language/vision/action mapping is a task association, not guaranteed robot capability.

Two source word clouds place warehouse logistics/precision agriculture/navigation on applications and sim-to-real/continuous learning/XAI among aims. Embodied AI appears in both; headings do not establish exclusive maturity or globally solved capabilities.
Summary lists biological origins, perceptrons, activations, MLP architecture, forward/loss/backprop, applications; no new technical equations.

Actual reference slide lists Bengio/Goodfellow/Courville Deep Learning (2017 as printed), Pratihar Soft Computing (2013), Vaswani et al. Attention Is All You Need (2017), and Szeliski Computer Vision (2022). The2017 Transformer reference contradicts interpreting the2020 timeline association as its invention year.

independentAnswers.independentDerivation: The printed timeline pairs LeNet with vision-guided pick/place and later language/vision models with manipulation. These are associations, not established invention dates.
A schematic timeline does not establish causal necessity or the exact year of every associated robotic deployment.
Observed diagram runs sensor inputs through weighted sum plus bias, then activation, then action signal.
The biological analogy explicitly maps dendrites to sensors, cell body to microcontroller, and axon to motor signal.
The table maps synapse to wire/CAN bus and threshold to trigger voltage.
Dot product plus bias is 2-2+0-1+0.5=-0.5.
The shown MP rule has implicit unit coefficients and a manually chosen threshold, not trained parameters.
Both 110 and 101 sum to two and satisfy the inclusive threshold two; 100 and 000 do not.
For three binary inputs, inclusive threshold three fires only on 111, implementing AND among the offered thresholds.
Changing inclusive threshold from one to two suppresses single-active-input patterns while retaining two-active patterns.
The displayed x1,x2,x3 order makes 101 looking fine, abnormal voice and verbal confirmation. This is toy logic only.
A known sum does not determine firing without the threshold; this page supplies no threshold.
Three ones sum to three, which meets threshold two and yields one.
No explicit weights means each shown contribution has coefficient one, not that every coefficient is zero.
Consistency with an illustrative binary rule is not clinical validation or evidence of medical accuracy.
Allowing real coordinates retains one affine threshold boundary; it does not make XOR linearly separable.
Positive XOR inequalities imply w1+w2+2b>=0, whereas the two negative inequalities imply the same sum is strictly negative, a contradiction.
Learnable coefficients improve fitting freedom without removing the representational limit of one affine boundary.
The MIT Press original and reissue descriptions identify the 1969 Minsky/Papert book as analysis of existing perceptrons, not invention of the earlier perceptron.
Substituting x0=1 and w0=-theta turns the threshold into the augmented sum compared inclusively with zero.
2*1-1*1-1=0, so the inclusive zero-threshold rule fires.
n counts measured input features; the three-feature illustration does not constrain n generally.
A fixed augmented input one makes its coefficient a feature-independent additive offset, while the coefficient remains learnable.
x1-2=0 places the boundary at x1=2.
The origin-to-hyperplane distance is abs(b)/norm(w); changing weight norm alters that distance even with fixed b.
The MP illustration uses fixed equal coefficients, whereas the perceptron learns individual feature weights and a bias.
Unequal sensitivity to normalized sensor features requires unequal coefficients, not merely an equal-weight sum with another threshold.
P denotes examples labeled one and N examples labeled zero, not the signs of their feature coordinates.
The described mistake-driven update leaves correctly classified examples unchanged.
Finite convergence requires a finite separable sample, fair repeated presentation and a positive fixed update step; it is not a guarantee for arbitrary data.
The actual algorithm inset adds x on a misclassified positive and subtracts x on a misclassified negative.
A zero score fires under the inclusive convention, so a negative example with zero score is a mistake and triggers subtraction.
The initial score is -2. Adding augmented x=(1,2,-1) to w=(0,-1,0) gives (1,1,-1), including the bias update.
Adding (1,0) to (-10,0) gives (-9,0); the improved score is still negative, so a single update need not correct a positive example.
For nonzero vectors a negative dot product means an obtuse angle. Adding x changes the same-example score by norm(x)^2.
Coordinates of x can be negative, so w+x need not increase every coordinate even though its dot product with x increases.
Step is nonlinear but has derivative zero off its threshold and no ordinary derivative at the discontinuity.
The inclusive step at zero is one, logistic sigmoid is one half, and tanh is zero.
tanh(-z)=-tanh(z), and tanh(0)=0, unlike the other listed activations.
Composing affine maps gives W2W1*x+(W2*b1+b2), still affine when activations are identities.
For finite exact inputs, exponential terms are positive and sigmoid/tanh never attain their limiting endpoints.
Exponentiating the logits gives (1,2,3); dividing by their sum six gives (1/6,2/6,3/6).
A common added logit constant contributes the same positive exponential factor to numerator and denominator, which cancels.
Independent binary attributes require independent marginal outputs; three sigmoids do not impose the mutually exclusive softmax sum constraint.
Signed hidden activations are a possible benefit, not a guarantee against saturation or universally better optimization.
sigmoid derivative p*(1-p) peaks at one quarter; tanh derivative 1-tanh(z)^2 peaks at one at zero.
Four maximum sigmoid factors with unit intervening weights give (1/4)^4=1/256.
The full chain includes weight Jacobians and path sums, so activation derivatives alone do not bound an arbitrary network gradient.
At fixed learning rate the update magnitude is proportional to gradient magnitude, so tiny gradients slow early-layer parameter changes.
Strictly on the negative half-line the ReLU slope is zero and the displayed leaky-ReLU slope is 0.01.
Both functions are continuous at zero but their left and right derivatives differ; software must choose a gradient convention.
A nonzero negative slope transmits a local gradient through negative inputs, without a network-wide nonvanishing guarantee.
For finite negative z, Phi(z) is strictly between zero and one, so z*Phi(z) remains negative.
The Gaussian-CDF GELU has a small negative minimum; -0.17 is a rounded value rather than its exact definition.
For positive z, ReLU and leaky ReLU equal z; finite exact Phi(z) lies between zero and one, so GELU lies strictly between zero and z.
Hidden weights and biases contribute 3*4+4=16; output weights and bias contribute 4+1=5, totaling 21.
Four output rows and three input columns require W1 shape 4x3 and b1/a1 shape 4x1.
The affine preactivation is (-1,1); elementwise ReLU gives (0,1).
The lecture distinguishes a single hidden layer from multiple hidden layers; output count and learning rate do not define depth.
One output from four hidden activations requires a 1x4 weight row and a scalar bias.
One sigmoid encodes the positive-class probability; the complementary class receives one minus that probability.
An identity output is not confined to a probability interval and can represent unbounded real-valued regression.
The output logit is 0.5*2-1*0-1=0, and sigmoid(0)=0.5.
The numbered source stages are forward prediction, loss evaluation, backward differentiation and parameter update.
The backward arrow denotes propagation of loss derivatives through earlier computational layers, not reversal of sensor time or inversion of the input.
Sum over only measured feature indices 1 through n plus b includes the bias once; also adding an augmented w0=b would duplicate it.
With the explicitly fixed parameters and running state, a forward pass computes successive affine maps and activations without optimizer updates.
The activation consumes the affine preactivation z, not a label or gradient.
The common pairings printed are cross-entropy for classification and mean squared error for continuous regression.
A frozen model can evaluate supervised loss on labeled validation samples without training; the printed training-only assertion is too restrictive.
The forward prediction needs inputs and parameters, while a supervised target-dependent loss also needs the target.
The printed no-minus expression reduces to log(1/2)=-ln2; adding the missing minus gives positive ln2.
For y=1 the printed expression is log p, which decreases without bound as the correct-class probability approaches zero.
For the stated second target class, negative log of its probability one half equals ln2.
Softmax transforms logits into normalized probabilities; categorical cross-entropy is a label-dependent scalar objective.
Errors are 1 and -2 meters, whose squared mean is (1+4)/2=2.5 square meters.
The outer index i runs through n observations; the inner j runs through K class probabilities and labels.
Backward differentiation produces parameter gradients; gradient descent applies the separate negative-gradient update.
Subtracting a positive learning rate times a positive gradient decreases that scalar parameter.
The illustration learns weights and biases while selecting the learning rate as a hyperparameter.
Setting n=1 removes averaging but leaves squared error. Multiplication by one half is a separate positive rescaling.
A positive constant rescaling preserves minimizers and rescales derivatives by the same factor, hence halving fixed-rate updates.
Differentiate half*(wx+b-y)^2: the residual multiplies x for w and one for b.
Using the cited half-squared affine-model loss, residual three times x=-2 gives dw=-6, while db=3.
The affine model derivative with respect to w is x, so x=0 kills that gradient while a nonzero residual remains in the bias derivative.
The chain rule through sigmoid adds sigmoid(z)*(1-sigmoid(z)) to both parameter-gradient paths.
The scalar displacement magnitude is eta*abs(gradient), so it depends on both factors.
A plateau may satisfy a stopping rule without proving global optimality, exact stationarity or held-out accuracy.
The source explicitly supplies x2, y10, w3, b1, eta0.1; the packet normalizes physical quantities for consistent numerical updates.
Torque divided by distance has units (N*m)/m=N, while the additive intercept retains torque units N*m.
One sample imposes only 2w+b=10, leaving a one-dimensional family of affine fits.
Zero residual for one illustrative sample does not establish collision avoidance across other states, speeds, dynamics or conditions.
Prediction 3*2+1=7; half-squared residual is (7-10)^2/2=4.5.
Ordinary single-example MSE is (7-10)^2=9, twice the half-squared loss.
At the shown initial state, residual -3 gives half-squared affine gradients (-3*2,-3)=(-6,-3).
A simultaneous gradient step computes both derivatives at the same old parameter vector before applying either change.
Subtracting 0.1*(-6,-3) from (3,1) gives (3.6,1.3).
The initial evaluation is labeled epoch one, so the next displayed evaluation follows one parameter update.
The actual reference slide identifies the Transformer paper as2017. A2020 association on the timeline is not a defensible invention date, independently confirmed by the original paper submission.
The actual static image has intercept1, slope3 and only the initial loss4.5 at epoch1; it does not display all five evolving curves.
The PDF problem uses braking torque10 Nm, while the graph axis and linked notebook identify motor speed, with the notebook target10 rad/s. These are distinct quantities.
Both w and b update: e_new=e-eta*e*(x^2+1)=0.5e. Squaring makes half-loss multiply by0.25.
Strict contraction requires abs(1-5eta)<1, equivalent to0<eta<0.4. Rates above0.2 can alternate sign while still contracting.
Convolutional filters exploit local spatial structure in the image/depth grid, rather than defining recurrent or all-pairs attention operations.
The actual diagram orders convolution, max pooling, convolution, max pooling, flatten, fully connected, output.
The second convolution is explicitly labeled8x8 and second pooling4x4.
Four by four spatial positions times C channels gives16C scalar values.
Even2x2 pooling yielding12 implies convolution output24. Valid stride1 gives28-k1+1=24, so k1=5;12-k2+1=8 gives k2=5.
In this digit illustration ten scores/features are compatible with distinguishing ten classes; the example output is7. It does not establish channels or a universal architecture.
The shown incoming arrows are current input xt and previous hidden state h(t-1).
Time-ordered IMU readings supply the temporal context the recurrent model is designed to summarize.
A learned hidden state can summarize useful previous inputs; it is not guaranteed exact, unlimited-duration storage.
The visibly added positional encoding represents order even when attention relates distant tokens; arbitrary permutations can change meaning.
Shifted-right inputs and causal masking prevent next-token predictions from reading their future target tokens.
The horizontal encoder-output connection enters the decoder attention block between masked self-attention and feedforward processing.
The decoder top is explicitly linear then softmax output probabilities.
Add and Norm denote residual addition/normalization and Nx denotes repeated encoder/decoder blocks.
Executing the command requires grounding the language relation in the visual scene and mapping it into robot action.
Warehouse logistics, precision agriculture and autonomous navigation are all visibly in the left application cloud.
Sim-to-real transfer, continuous learning and explainable AI are visibly in the right aims cloud.
Embodied AI appears in both clouds, demonstrating overlapping illustrative categories rather than mutually exclusive proven maturity classes.
The actual left cloud says Surgical Robotics and the right says Advanced Surgical Robots; neither is a guarantee of completed capability.
The source explicitly assigns3.0 and1.0 and draws no random values for these parameters; calling seed does not cause those assignments.
History is appended before assigning updated weights, so index0 is w3,b1,half-loss4.5.
range(1,6) executes five iterations, each recording one pre-update loss and making one update.
Independent execution of all five original updates gives w4.1625,b1.58125 and2w+b=9.90625; the final stored frame is the preceding state.
The prefix ending before i+1 and integer range1 through i+1 both have i+1 points, matching the current frame.
The source creates the text artist before the callback references epoch_text.set_text, supplying the missing binding.
The source setup includes !pip and %matplotlib, which require IPython processing rather than direct ordinary Python parsing.
The final stored frame evaluates4.125*4+1.5625=18.0625 above y-limit15. Plot clipping does not alter that computed prediction.
